newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian second-tier companies look to ADRs.
newsitem.headline: Russian second-tier companies look to ADRs.

text.p: The Russian equity market will benefit from less liquid companies joining leading firms in seeking to issue American Depositary Receipts on shares, drawing in investors and raiding liquidity, analysts said on Wednesday.
"There will be a lot more ADRs coming. It probably will continue to drive up prices in shares that have been illiquid," said one analyst at a Western brokerage in Moscow.

The number of firms planning ADRs has grown steadily since the first Russian companies received permission last year to issue the receipts, which allow shares to be traded abroad and ease custody and settlement problems common in emerging markets.
The Bank of New York, which has acted as the depositary bank for all approximately 15 ADR issues by Russian companies so far, estimates another 15 companies will issue ADRs this year.

Russia's largest company UES launched a global depositary receipt (GDR) on Monday, bouncing its share price up to a record $0.3410 from $0.2798 on Thursday, the last day it traded before the announcement. UES was trading at $0.2900 on Wednesday.
Retailer TsUM was last month granted a rule 12g3-2b exemption, a prerequisite for issuing level-one ADRs.

Russia's biggest oil producer LUKoil which had one of the first Russian level-one ADR programmes, is now working on plans for level-three ADRs early next year, which will allow it to raise new capital from investors.

But while some of Russia's biggest companies are among the ranks of those pushing ahead with ADRs, companies with less liquid shares, including some trading on the second tier of the Russian Trading System, are also looking more seriously at the benefits of ADR issues.
"Second-tiers are increasingly interested in depositary receipts," said Christopher Kearns, head of the Bank of New York's depositary receipt development programme in Russia.
"It's a natural trend that we've seen around the world that blue chips lead the depositary receipt market and second-tier companies follow."

Uralmash, a heavy equipment maker located near Yekaterinburg in the Ural mountains, and whose shares do not trade on either RTS segment, said on Tuesday that holding company Uralmash Industries was planning an ADR issue on a private share placement in the autumn.
Regional telecoms Uralsvyazinform and Tyumentelekom, which have been registering strong investor interest in recent weeks, are also mulling plans for ADR issues.

"Many companies are second-tier only because people don't know about them. ADR programmes do a lot to raise their prominence," said Christopher Smart, Director of Research for Pioneer First Investment Group.
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission must conduct a thorough review of a company's accounts before granting permission for an ADR issue.

But analysts said companies which had gone through the rigorous examination had no reason to be disappointed in the results, which included higher international profile, increased liquidity and, often, growing share prices.

"It's a good mechanism for Russian companies to present themselves to foreign investors and...for investors to get exposure to Russian equities," said Smart. "In each case where a company has an ADR programme the price has tended to rise."
ADRs also increase Russia's access to other financial tools.

"There are more and more Russian companies that understand that access to international capital markets is well worth the trouble of disclosure and transparency," said Jim Nail, director of research for Russia at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
A $200-million five-year convertible bond issued by LUKoil last month was heavily oversubscribed and Gazprom, which issued ADRs at the end of last year, plans a Eurobond this year.
And analysts said ADRs would benefit not only individual shares but the market as a whole.
"ADRs will help raise prices and raise liquidity in the market overall, I don't think they will be the only driving force but they will certainly make an important contribution," said Smart.
